summary.headline: Standalone Q4 FY26 sales hit a record INR1,522 crore (+24% YoY) and FY26 EBITDA margin rose 90 bps to 13.1%.
summary.overview: Kirloskar Oil Engines reported its highest-ever quarterly standalone sales of INR1,522 crore in Q4 FY26, up 24% YoY, with growth across all B2B units. Standalone EBITDA rose 27% to INR193 crore and margin expanded 30 bps to 12.6%. For FY26, standalone net sales grew 25% to INR5,604 crore and EBITDA grew 33% to INR737 crore, with margin at 13.1%. Management announced a new INR1,400 crore Kagal capex for about 20,000 engines (mainly high-horsepower) over two years, on top of the earlier INR700 crore programme for 50,000 engines due by April 2027.

segments.name: Financial services (Arka Fincap)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR221 crore, +8% YoY; segment PBT INR28 crore, +157%. FY26 AUM INR7,947 crore (+10%), NII INR266 crore (+11%), PAT INR69 crore; branches scaled from 34 to 137; GNPA 1.2% and NNPA 0.3%.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated the USD 2 billion company goal by FY30 and said industrial and aftermarket are important to reaching it.

Management said it saw no margin deterioration; operating leverage is expected to build as new capacity and international traction ramp, with the full intention to maximise it (no timeline given beyond 'soon').
Management expects some raw-material cost inflation to be passed on to the market, but would not quantify any FY26 price hikes or Q4 price increases.
Management sees the NPCIL order (INR798 crore combined with marine order) executing by 2029; billing and revenue recognition on it had not started yet.

Management said the new Kagal capex of about INR1,400 crore is to be capitalised over the next two years, with revenue expected to flow to the P&L after that. The peak revenue potential is about INR5,000-6,000 crore at a 4x asset turn.
capex_capacity: New Kagal capex of about INR1,400 crore over two years for about 20,000 engines, mainly HHP, including a new building on the existing Kagal site (no land acquisition) and new lines; described as fully growth capex, not replacement.
Earlier INR700 crore Kagal programme adds about 50,000 engines via new lines in the existing plant and is due online by April 2027.
Current engine capacity is about 1,35,000 units; asset turn guided at 4-5% depending on node.
Management said it is ready to build engines on gas, ethanol, methanol or hydrogen blends, but said there was nothing meaningful yet in alternative-fuel gensets demand.
The Netherlands subsidiary and Kirloskar Advanced Systems Pvt Ltd (defence and systems integration) were set up, though management said these describe possible future scope rather than current plans.
demand_pricing: Overall Indian diesel generator market grew 18% to ~1,79,000 units in FY26 (including telecom); KOEL grew 41%, selling over 50,000 units.
High-horsepower share is approaching double digits from negligible a couple of years ago. Optiprime sold a few hundred units in FY26; the company has sold units up to 3,000 kVA.
Single-engine capability: 6.3 MW (~8,000 kVA) for NPCIL; data-centre single-engine up to 1,650 kVA; management expects to go higher.

Management expects demand to remain strong, with some material-cost inflation hard for industry to absorb. Management called the current period turbulent and said Middle East effects were not visible in Q4.
R&D is about 2% of sales, and management said R&D expense rises with sales.

qa_highlights.question: Can you attribute export growth and say whether it is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fluid Dynamics had a strong year and Power Gen is a big international opportunity. It said the company sees the growth as sustainable once it is entrenched in a market; it reported over INR1,000 crore in international gross sales.

qa_highlights.question: Power Gen volume/price split, FY26 HHP sales number, and HHP contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give the volume/price split, the HHP sales number, or HHP share of Power Gen, and described HHP only qualitatively.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the new 20,000-engine capex (INR1,400 crore) higher than the 50,000-engine capex (INR700 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the new programme includes a new building on the existing Kagal site and new lines and equipment for higher-HP engines, while the earlier INR700 crore added lines in the existing plant.

qa_highlights.question: Margin sustainability and when operating leverage will show, given higher other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no margin deterioration and some nodes showed operating leverage. It said most investments were made, and larger leverage is expected as new capacity and international traction ramp.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to the Middle East (reported as 40-50% of exports) and short-term disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no impact was seen in Q4 and the next quarters were hard to call. It also said there were no specific short-term disruptions in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre contribution and the Arka asset-quality and NPCIL order status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said data-centre contribution would be premature to disclose; it targets double-digit share of Power Gen. Arka GNPA was 1.2% and NNPA 0.3% at March 2026. The NPCIL order runs to 2029 with billing not yet started.

risks_watch: Raw-material inflation (copper, pig iron) with no disclosed FY26 price-hike quantum; management says some cost pass-through is likely.
Middle East exposure: reportedly 40-50% of export revenue; no Q4 impact, but management would not forecast later quarters.
Execution of the INR1,400 crore and INR700 crore capex programmes, with the new capacity timeline and asset turn at 4-5%.
Arka: 137 branches with rapid growth and FY26 PAT of INR69 crore; asset quality to be tracked as the secured retail book scales.
Management withheld the HHP split, product pipeline, and Power Gen volume/price split, which limits modelling visibility.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the headline numbers and multi-year growth, but guarded on specifics. Management declined several questions (HHP mix, volume/price split, pricing quantum, product pipeline, data-centre contribution) and kept geopolitical and raw-material outlook qualitative.
